key_insight: A hip-exoskeleton controller co-trained with a simulated human reduced walking metabolic cost in new users without per-user tuning.
engineering_relevance: Simulation-based co-adaptation offers a route to population-level assistive controllers and enables assistance objectives to be screened before human testing.
method: Co-trained a 304-muscle human model and bilateral hip-exoskeleton policy using two-stage multi-agent reinforcement learning.
Randomized anatomy, gait, and speed; restricted controller inputs to delayed hip kinematics and past commands.
Compared metabolic-only rewards with metabolic-plus-mechanical-power shaping.
evidence_signal: In eight healthy adults walking at 1.25 m/s, the metabolic-only policy reduced net metabolic rate by 18.3 ± 6.6% versus Passive and 7.4 ± 10.0% versus No-Exo; simulated reductions were 13.8% with metabolic-only rewards versus 8.8% with added power shaping.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to eight healthy adults at one walking speed, and only six achieved a metabolic cost below their No-Exo baseline.
paper_title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
